==English== ===Etymology=== From {{inh|en|enm|whisperen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hwisprian||to mutter, murmur, whisper}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*hwisprōn}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*hwisprōną||to hiss, whistle, whisper}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ḱweys-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*ḱwey-||to hiss, whistle, whisper}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|wisperen||to whisper}}, {{cog|de|wispern||to mumble, whisper}}. Related also to {{cog|da|hviske||to whisper}}, {{cog|is|hvískra||to whisper}}, {{cog|nb|hviske}}, {{m|nb|kviskre||to whisper}}, {{cog|nn|kviskre}}, {{m|nn|kviskra||to whisper}}, {{cog|sv|viska||to whisper}}. More at {{cog|en|whistle}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ˈ(h)wɪspə/|a=RP}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈ(h)wɪspɚ/|a=GenAm}} * {{audio|en|en-us-whisper.ogg|a=GA}} * {{rhymes|en|ɪspə(ɹ)|s=2}} ===Noun=== {{wp|+ing}} {{en-noun}} # {{senseid|en|Q1434962}} The act of [[speak]]ing in a [[quiet]] [[voice]], especially without [[vibration]] of the [[vocal cord]]s; the sound thus produced. #: {{alti|en|mul:W}} #: {{ux|en|I spoke in a near '''whisper'''.}} #* {{RQ:Stevenson Treasure Island|text="Now, look here, Jim Hawkins," he said, in a steady '''whisper''', that was no more than audible.}} # {{lb|en|usually|in the plural}} A [[rumor]]. #: {{ux|en|There are '''whispers''' of rebellion all around.}} # {{lb|en|figurative}} A [[faint]] [[trace]] or [[hint]] (of something). #: {{ux|en|The soup had just a '''whisper''' of basil.}} # A [[low]] [[rustling]] [[sound]], like that of the [[wind]] in [[leaves]]. # {{lb|en|internet}} A [[private]] [[message]] to an [[individual]] in a [[chat room]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=2002|author=Ralph Schroeder|title=The Social Life of Avatars|page=218 |passage=The invisibility of private interactions in the form of '''whispers''' resolved an ethical concern in the research but reduced our ability to gauge the volume of interaction {{...}}}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2004|author=Caroline A. Haythornthwaite; Michelle M. Kazmer|title=Learning, Culture and Community in Online Education|page=179 |passage=Anyone logged in to the chat room can click on an individual name, highlighting it, and send a message — a '''''whisper''''' — that will be seen only by the selected person.}} # {{lb|en|occult}} A [[projection]] of [[intention]] and influence caused by sending thoughts or desires outward through softly-spoken words or subtle mental or energetic [[means]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1965|author=Attila Zohar|title=Kings Cross Black Magic|location=Sydney|publisher=Horwitz Publications|page=66|passage="Witches feel that anyone who is against them has to be destroyed. The method is to give the victim what we call a ''whispering''. It is similar to the aborigine ceremony in Australia of singing someone to death. The witches gather in a circle and focus their hate on the persons they have in mind. These vibrations from their minds and voices carry '''''whispers''''' to the one who they are working against."}} ====Derived terms==== {{col|en|whisperless|in a pig's whisper|kissper|pig's whisper|whisper network|stage whisper|a whisper down the lane|whisper campaign|whisper porn|whisperhood|whisperous|by a whisper|whispersome|whispery|whisper interpreting|whisper test|Chinese whispers|semiwhisper}} ====Translations==== {{trans-top|act of speaking in a quiet voice}} * Akan: * Arabic: * Armenian: * Asturian: * Azerbaijani: * Belarusian: * Bikol: * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Cebuano: * Chinese: * Czech: * Danish: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Estonian: * Faroese: * Finnish: * French: * Galician: * Georgian: * German: * Greek: * Hawaiian: * Hebrew: * Hiligaynon: * Hungarian: * Icelandic: * Ido: * Ilocano: * Indonesian: * Irish: * Italian: * Japanese: * Javanese: * Kapampangan: * Kinaray-a: * Korean: * Kurdish: * Latgalian: * Latin: * Latvian: * Lithuanian: * Luxembourgish: * Macedonian: * Malay: * Mongolian: * Norwegian: * Old English: * Persian: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Romanian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|шёпот|m}} * Sami: * Scottish Gaelic: * Serbo-Croatian: * Slovak: * Slovene: * Spanish: * Swedish: * Tagalog: * Tajik: * Tamil: * Telugu: * Thai: * Turkish: * Turkmen: * Ugaritic: * Ukrainian: * Vietnamese: * Welsh: * Woiwurrung: * Yiddish: * Yogad: * Yoruba: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|rumor}} * Asturian: * Bulgarian: * Finnish: * Galician: * Italian: * Malay: * Spanish: * Tamil: * Turkish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|faint trace or hint}} * Asturian: * Bulgarian: * Finnish: * Spanish: * Tamil: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|internet: private message in a chat room}} * Finnish: {{trans-bottom}} ===Verb=== [[File:USCGC Polar Star returns to Wellington - March 20th, 2026 (55157704619) (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|A man '''whispers''' to a woman]] {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[speak]] [[softly]] or [[under one's breath]], so as to be [[hear]]d only by one [[near at hand]]; to [[utter]] [[word]]s without [[sonant]] [[breath]]; to [[talk]] without that [[vibration]] of the [[vocal cord]]s which gives [[sonorous]], or [[vocal]], [[sound]]. #: {{syn|en|breathe}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[say]] (something) [[softly]] or [[under one's breath]], so as to be [[hear]]d only by one [[near at hand]]; to [[utter]] (something) without [[sonant]] [[breath]], without that [[vibration]] of the [[vocal cord]]s which gives [[sonorous]], or [[vocal]], [[sound]]. #: {{syn|en|breathe}} #* {{RQ:en:New York Times|author=Ira Berkow|title=DRAMA IN 'STENGELESE: YOU CAN LOOK IT UP|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1981/04/15/sports/drama-in-stengelese-you-can-look-it-up.html|date=15-04-1981|passage=Whether he '''whispered''' sweet nothings to her in Stengelese is not known, but he did call her "the best catch I ever made in my career."}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[mention]] [[privately]] and [[confidentially]], or in a [[#Noun|whisper]]. #* {{RQ:Bentley Confutation of Atheism|passage=They might buzz and '''whisper''' it one to another.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To make a [[low]], [[sibilant]] [[sound]]. #* {{RQ:Thomson Spring|year=1768|passage=the hollow, '''whispering''' breeze}} #* {{RQ:Tennyson In Memoriam|XXXVII|57|{{...}} hear thy laurel '''whisper''' sweet
About the ledges of the hill.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[speak]] with [[suspicion]] or [[timorous]] [[caution]]; to [[converse]] in [[#Noun|whisper]]s, as in [[secret]] [[plotting]]. #* {{RQ:KJV|Psalms|41|7|passage=All that hate me '''whisper''' together against me.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To [[address]] in a [[#Noun|whisper]], or [[low]] [[voice]]. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare King John|IV|ii|passage=and '''whisper''' one another in the ear}} #* {{RQ:Keble Christian Year|passage=where gentlest breezes '''whisper''' souls distressed}} # {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To [[prompt]] [[secretly]] or [[cautiously]]; to [[inform]] [[privately]]. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 8|I|ii|passage=He came to '''whisper''' Wolsey.}} #* {{RQ:Scott Antiquary|volume=I|chapter=XIII|page=289|passage=[A] simple youth '''whispered''' me that he was an ''Illuminé'', and carried on an intercourse with the invisible world.}} # {{lb|en|internet}} To send a [[private]] [[message]] to an [[individual]] in a [[chat room]]. # To exercise [[skill]] in [[tame|taming]] or [[train]]ing a creature. # {{lb|en|occult}} To [[project]] intention and [[influence]] events by sending thoughts or desires [[outward]] through softly-spoken words or [[subtle]] [[mental]] or [[energetic]] means;
